ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an ideal operational amplifier circuit. The non-inverting input terminal “+” of the op-amp is connected to a voltage-dividing node composed of 10kΩ and 30kΩ: the input ui first passes through 10kΩ to this node, and this node is then grounded through 30kΩ. The inverting input terminal “-” of the op-amp is connected to the feedback network: this node is grounded through 10kΩ, and is connected to the output terminal uo through a 30kΩ resistor. Reasoning: The non-inverting terminal voltage is obtained by input voltage division, V+ = ui × 30kΩ / (10kΩ + 30kΩ) = 3ui/4. An ideal op-amp under negative feedback has V- = V+. The inverting terminal corresponds to a standard non-inverting amplifier feedback network, whose closed-loop gain is 1 + Rf/Rg = 1 + 30kΩ/10kΩ = 4. Therefore uo = 4V+ = 4 × 3ui/4 = 3ui, so the voltage gain uo/ui = 3.

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, what is the voltage gain of the ideal operational amplifier circuit?

method.method_draft: From the image, identify the circuit as a non-inverting amplifier whose + terminal receives a divided version of ui: V+ = ui · 30k/(10k + 30k) = 3ui/4. The inverting side has Rg = 10 kΩ to ground and Rf = 30 kΩ from output to the − terminal, so for an ideal op amp with negative feedback, uo = (1 + Rf/Rg) V+ = (1 + 30k/10k)(3ui/4) = 4 · 3ui/4 = 3ui. Therefore the voltage gain uo/ui is 3.
